questions.question: What is the primary function of hemoglobin in the body?
options: To transport oxygen from lungs to cells
questions.explanation: Hemoglobin is the protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen from the lungs to every cell in the body.

questions.question: Which of the following is a rich source of heme iron (most easily absorbed)?
questions.explanation: Heme iron is found in animal foods like beef liver, chicken, and fish. It is more easily absorbed (15–35%) than non-heme iron from plant sources.

questions.question: Why do women of reproductive age need more iron than men?
questions.explanation: Women lose iron through monthly menstruation. The average woman loses 30–40 mL of blood per period, resulting in approximately 200–250 mg of iron lost per year.

questions.question: What does a low MCV (Mean Corpuscular Volume) indicate in iron deficiency anemia?
options: Red blood cells are too large
Red blood cells are small and pale
There are too many white blood cells
questions.explanation: In iron deficiency anemia, MCV is low (<80 fL), meaning red blood cells are microcytic (small) and hypochromic (pale) due to insufficient hemoglobin.

questions.question: Which drink can BLOCK iron absorption when consumed with meals?
questions.explanation: Coffee and tea contain tannins and polyphenols that bind to iron and reduce absorption. Orange juice, rich in vitamin C, actually enhances absorption.

questions.question: How long does it typically take for hemoglobin to return to normal after starting iron treatment?
questions.explanation: While energy may improve in 1–2 weeks, hemoglobin takes 2–3 months to return to normal. Iron stores (ferritin) take 6 months to fully replenish.

questions.question: Which vitamin enhances the absorption of non-heme iron from plant foods?
questions.explanation: Vitamin C converts non-heme iron into a more absorbable form. Good combinations include lentils with tomatoes, or fortified cereal with orange juice.

questions.question: What is the name of the condition where a person craves non-food items like ice or dirt?
questions.explanation: Pica is the craving and eating of non-food items such as ice, dirt, or starch. It is strongly associated with iron deficiency.

questions.question: During pregnancy, a woman's daily iron need increases to approximately:
questions.explanation: Pregnant women need 27 mg/day of iron — the highest recommendation of any adult group — due to increased blood volume and fetal development.

questions.question: Which group is at the HIGHEST risk for iron deficiency anemia?
questions.explanation: Women with heavy menstrual periods (menorrhagia) lose significantly more blood — sometimes 2–3 times the average amount — dramatically increasing their risk of iron deficiency anemia.
